fields.aka: Mādhavendra Purī, Mādhava Purī, Purī Gosvāmī, Śrīpāda Mādhavendra
fields.disappearance: Phālguna śukla dvādaśī (Gauḍīya calendar); at Remuṇā according to tradition
fields.place: Travelled all over India; revealed Gopāla on Govardhana; Remuṇā (Kṣīra-corā Gopīnātha); Purī
fields.guru: Śrī Lakṣmīpati (Gauḍīya guru-praṇālī; the link with the Mādhva line is discussed by historians)
fields.disciples: Īśvara Purī, Advaita Ācārya (dīkṣā), Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi, Paramānanda Purī, Raṅga Purī, Brahmānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Keśava Bhāratī, Kṛṣṇānanda Purī, Rāmacandra Purī (rejected), Nṛsiṁha Tīrtha, Raghupati Upādhyāya, Sukhānanda Purī, Saṅkarṣaṇa Purī, the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa of Mathurā, Mādhava Miśra; Nityānanda revered him as His guru
fields.works: Five verses in the Padyāvalī (79, 96, 164, 286, 330); the verse «ayi dīna-dayārdra nātha» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 4.197)
fields.notes:
Root of the tree of prema-bhakti (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.10); parama-guru of Lord Caitanya; «the first stage-manager of bhakti-rasa» (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Revealed Gopāla on Govardhana and held the Annakūṭa; Gopīnātha of Remuṇā stole sweet rice for him (Kṣīra-corā); brought sandalwood from Purī, which by Gopāla's order went on Gopīnātha's body (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 4). Initiated Advaita at Śāntipura; blessed Jagannātha Miśra and Śacī. Met Nityānanda in the West: Nityānanda treated him as guru, he treated Nityānanda as a friend (Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi 9; Bhakti-ratnākara 5.2330-2332). Rejected Rāmacandra Purī; blessed Īśvara Purī with prema for his service at the end (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 8). Died repeating «ayi dīna-dayārdra nātha»; Kiśorī dāsa wrote the Bindu-prakāśa on it (1702 Śaka). His Gopāla is now at Nāthdvārā.

Paramparā (Gauḍīya Sampradāya chart, 04-11-2026): dīkṣā line from Madhva — succession according to Baladeva; the link with Madhva is disputed by historians.

fields.appearance: Jyaiṣṭha pūrṇimā, at Kumārahaṭṭa (Hālisahar) (B. V. Tīrtha)
fields.disappearance: Māgha kṛṣṇa dvādaśī (Gauḍīya calendar, which counts months from full moon to full moon: Phālguna/Govinda kṛṣṇa dvādaśī)
fields.place: Born at Kumārahaṭṭa (Hālisahar), on the Gaṅgā north of Calcutta
fields.disciples: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu (dīkṣā at Gayā); Govinda; Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī; Nityānanda according to the Prema-vilāsa (24)
fields.works: Śrī Kṛṣṇa-līlāmṛta (not found; two verses in the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi); verses in the Padyāvalī
fields.notes:
Son of Śyāmasundara Ācārya, a Rāḍhī brāhmaṇa of Kumārahaṭṭa (Prema-vilāsa 23; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Mādhavendra Purī's dearest disciple: served him at the end and was blessed with prema (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 8.28-31). In Navadvīpa stayed at Gopīnātha Ācārya's house, taught Gadādhara his Kṛṣṇa-līlāmṛta and asked Nimāi to correct it (Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi 11.70-126). Gave Lord Caitanya the ten-syllable mantra at Gayā (Ādi 17.46-112). Before leaving this world sent Govinda and Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī to serve the Lord (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 10.131-148).

The record had Nityānanda among his disciples: so the Prema-vilāsa (24); the Caitanya-bhāgavata says Nityānanda took Mādhavendra as His guru.

fields.name: Śrī Keśava Bhāratī
fields.aka: Keśava Bhāratī, Kālīnātha Ācārya (before sannyāsa), Bhāratī Gosāñi
fields.place: Kuliyā (Navadvīpa); gave sannyāsa to Lord Caitanya at Kāṭoyā
fields.notes:
A Vārendra brāhmaṇa of Kuliyā named Kālīnātha Ācārya; disciple of Mādhavendra Purī (Prema-vilāsa 23). Gave sannyāsa and the name Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya to Lord Caitanya at Kāṭoyā (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 28.105-174). Brother: Balabhadra. Families of Cũcuḍā, Denuḍa (Bhāratīra puṣkariṇī) and other places call themselves his descendants (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Sāndīpani Muni, who gave Kṛṣṇa the sacred thread; some say Akrūra (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 52, 117).

The record had Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī as his disciple: that came from Prakāśānanda's words to the Lord («You are a disciple of Keśava Bhāratī»).

fields.place: Stayed for a time in Jagannātha Purī; had a maṭha in Vārāṇasī (B. V. Tīrtha)
fields.notes:
The rejected disciple of Mādhavendra Purī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna): he told his guru, crying in separation, to remember Brahman, and was driven away (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 8.17-31). In Purī the Lord bowed to him as His guru's godbrother; he pressed Jagadānanda to eat and then blamed him, and blamed the Lord's eating, so that the Lord halved His meals; when he left, the devotees felt relieved (Antya 8). Named in the Vaiṣṇava-vandanās (Jīva 125, Devakīnandana 45, Vṛndāvana dāsa 43).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vibhīṣaṇa; but Lord Caitanya said Jaṭilā, Rādhā's mother-in-law, entered him (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 92-93).
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, «Sri Chaitanya: His Associates».

fields.name: Śrī Raṅga Purī
fields.place: Met Lord Caitanya at Paṇḍharpur; then Dvārakā; ended his life in Nīlācala
fields.notes: Disciple of Mādhavendra Purī. At Paṇḍharpur he received Lord Caitanya, remembered eating at Jagannātha Miśra's house with Mādhavendra, and told the Lord that Viśvarūpa (Śaṅkarāraṇya) had attained perfection there (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9.282-303). The record had «Mādhavendra Purī» as his disciple by mistake.

fields.name: Viṣṇu Purī
fields.place: Born at Tiraudhi in Tirhut (Mithilā); lived at Kāśī near Bindumādhava
fields.guru: Jayadharma of the Mādhva line (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna); some say Mādhavendra Purī
fields.notes:
One of the nine sannyāsī roots of the tree of bhakti (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.13-14). Before sannyāsa Viṣṇuśarmā of the Karmaha family of Tiraudhi, Tirhut. Jagannātha asked in a dream for his «garland of jewels», the Bhakti-ratnāvalī, and it was put on Him verse by verse (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). His date is discussed (Haraprasāda Śāstrī: 1633; manuscripts of 1595; S. K. De: long before Lord Caitanya; Buchanan Hamilton heard of him at Purnea).

Guru: the Abhidhāna says Jayadharma, «some say Mādhavendra Purī»; the record put Mādhavendra first.

fields.name: Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita (Gaura-Govinda)
fields.aka: Kāśīśvara, Kāśīśvara Paṇḍit, Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī, Kāśīśvara Gosāñi
fields.disappearance: Kārtika śukla caturdaśī (Gauḍīya calendar; one text: Āśvina pūrṇimā)
fields.place: Cātarā, near Śrīrāmpur; Vṛndāvana (Śrī Gaura-Govinda beside Govindadeva)
fields.guru: Not given in the Abhidhāna (a devotee of Lord Caitanya); those who take him as the same as Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī: Īśvara Purī
fields.disciples: Govinda Gosāñi (pūjārī of Śrī Govinda, Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 8.66); the son of Mahādeva Bhaṭṭācārya, his nephew
fields.notes:
A devotee of Lord Caitanya, of Cātarā; by the Lord's order went to Vṛndāvana and installed Śrī Gaura-Govinda, the deity the Lord gave him as His own self, beside Śrī Govindadeva (Bhakti-ratnākara 2.440-444, 6.444, 479; Sādhana-dīpikā 2.41). His nephew Rudra Paṇḍita was the first priest of Vallabhapur; father Vāsudeva Bhaṭṭācārya, of the Kāñjilāl family (Śrīla Prabhupāda).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kelimañjarī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

The Abhidhāna and Kavi Karṇapūra keep him apart from Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī, Īśvara Purī's disciple who served the Lord in Purī (Bhṛṅgāra), who has his own record; Śrīla Prabhupāda and others take them as one. The record «Kāśīśvara Paṇḍit» (the one the Gauḍīya calendar named) was joined to this one (06-11-2026); this record was in the tree under Mādhavendra Purī, without a source.

fields.name: Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī (disciple of Īśvara Purī)
fields.aka: Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī Gosvāmī, Kāśīśvara Gosāñi, Brahmacārī Kāśīśvara
fields.notes:
Of Lord Caitanya's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.138); disciple of Īśvara Purī, who with Govinda sent him to serve the Lord in Purī; very strong, he kept the crowds back when the Lord went to see Jagannātha (Madhya 10.131-148; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). See Bhaktamāla 20.12.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Bhṛṅgāra, Kṛṣṇa's servant; also the sakhī Śaśirekhā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 137, 166).

The Abhidhāna keeps him apart from Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita, who took Gaura-Govinda to Vṛndāvana (his own record); Śrīla Prabhupāda and others take them as one.

fields.name: Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa of Mathurā
fields.notes: An elderly brāhmaṇa of the Sanoḍiyā community of Mathurā, made a disciple by Mādhavendra Purī, who ate at his house; he received Lord Caitanya at Mathurā, cooked for Him, and went with Him round Vraja (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 17.163-188). The record had «Mādhavendra Purī» also as his disciple by mistake.

fields.guru: Not known (a Māyāvādī sannyāsī of Śaṅkara's line); took shelter of Lord Caitanya at Kāśī
fields.notes:
Leader of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs of Kāśī (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 3.37-40); criticised Lord Caitanya, was won over at the meeting of the sannyāsīs (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 7) and at Bindumādhava took His shelter, told to study the Bhāgavatam (Madhya 17.104-143, 25.5-160; Bhaktamāla 22.7).

The record had «Śrī Keśava Bhāratī» as his guru: that came from his words to the Lord («You are a disciple of Keśava Bhāratī»). Not Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī, who has his own record (Whisper, 06-11-2026: two persons; the Gauḍīya Maṭha holds they were one). Not Prakāśānanda, disciple of Advaita.
A disciple of Mādhavendra Purī (Jīva Gosvāmī, Vaiṣṇava-vandanā, p. 290). Jīva Gosvāmī names him as Nityānanda's guru; other sources: Mādhavendra Purī, Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha or Īśvara Purī.

fields.name: Raghupati Upādhyāya
fields.guru: Mādhavendra Purī (in the lists of his disciples)
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa of Tirhut (Mithilā) (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 19.92). When Lord Caitanya stayed at Vallabha Bhaṭṭa's house at Āḍāila, Raghupati came and took shelter at His feet; the Lord, delighted, heard him speak of Kṛṣṇa and embraced him (Madhya 19.93-107). Named among Mādhavendra Purī's disciples in the record of Mādhavendra.

fields.name: Brahmānanda Purī
fields.notes: One of the nine sannyāsīs who are the roots of the tree of bhakti (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.13); a disciple of Mādhavendra Purī who was with him when he met Nityānanda (Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi 9.170); later a sannyāsī companion of Lord Caitanya in Purī.

A disciple of Mādhavendra Purī; one of the nine sannyāsī roots of the tree of bhakti («Viṣṇu Purī, Keśava Purī, Purī Kṛṣṇānanda, Śrī Nṛsiṁha Tīrtha and Purī Sukhānanda», Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.13-14); a sannyāsī companion of Lord Caitanya. In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: one of the nine yogīndras, Jayanteya (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 98-100; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).
Disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī; one of the nine sannyāsī roots of the tree of bhakti («Purī Kṛṣṇānanda», Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.13-14).
Disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī; one of the nine sannyāsī roots of the tree of bhakti («Purī Sukhānanda», Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.13-14).
A disciple of Mādhavendra Purī (Jayānanda, Caitanya-maṅgala 34).

Father: Vilāsa Ācārya. Wife: Ratnāvatī Devī (Navakumārī Devī). Sons: Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī, Vāṇīnātha Paṇḍita. A Vārendra brāhmaṇa of Beleṭi, Chittagong; a disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī (Prema-vilāsa 22); close friend of Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi — «Puṇḍarīka and Mādhava studied together: one soul, only the bodies two» (Prema-vilāsa 20) (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Mādhava Miśra» 1).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: a manifestation of Vṛṣabhānu; his wife Ratnāvatī was Kīrtidā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 57).

The record had «Caṇḍīlīlā» among his works: that is the other Mādhava Miśra (Mādhavācārya) of Saptagrāma and Nanyāpur, who wrote it in 1501 (Abhidhāna, «Mādhava Miśra» 3); the second part of his text is about him.
